_comment: AI GAME COMPANY license registry (master prompt section 8). Every AI model, asset, sound, texture and 3D model used by any game is registered here. Section 38: an entry with status UNKNOWN must never ship inside a released APK.
_rule_code_vs_weights: Section 8: an open-source CODE license does not imply the same license for MODEL WEIGHTS. The two are verified separately and get separate entries.

The user confirmed on 2026-09-02 that these are their own images and that commercial use is permitted, so derived work may ship. Two things still hold. (1) The renders carry an AI-generation watermark; if the generating service's terms ever turn out to restrict commercial use, that is a licence question about the service, not about this entry, and it should be re-verified rather than assumed. What ships today is not a crop of these images: it is a procedurally drawn sprite built to match them (Assets/Common/Character/Generated/Dori.png), which the user may later replace by dropping a cut-out PNG at Assets/Common/Art/Runner/player.png.

entries.name: Gemma 4 26B (Q4_K_M) - pulled into local Ollama
entries.source: ollama pull gemma4:26b - recorded in HARDWARE_PROFILE.json ollamaApi.models
entries.version: 25.2B parameters, Q4_K_M, 17.33 GB of weights, pulled 2026-08-31
entries.redistribution_rules: unknown
entries.notes: Present on the machine but NOT usable, for two independent reasons. (1) Licence: unread. Gemma releases have historically shipped under Google's own Gemma Terms of Use plus a Prohibited Use Policy rather than a plain OSI licence, and section 8 says weights are licensed separately from code - so the actual terms for THIS model ID must be read before any output of it is used. Family resemblance is not a licence. (2) Size: 17.33 GB of weights against 15.71 GB of total RAM on a machine with no dedicated GPU. It exceeds the whole machine and cannot be loaded, whatever else is closed - 'orchestrator ollama' reports this. Recommended action: remove it (ollama rm gemma4:26b) to reclaim ~17 GB, and pull a 7B-class Q4 model instead, after checking THAT model ID's licence. OllamaClient.generate() refuses this ID today because it is not APPROVED here. REMOVED FROM THE MACHINE, verified 2026-09-02: `ollama rm gemma4:26b` answered "model not found" and `orchestrator ollama --list`, which queries the live Ollama API, printed "no models installed". HARDWARE_PROFILE.json still lists it because it was generated 2026-09-01 01:14 and has not been regenerated since - re-run detect-environment.ps1 to correct that. The entry stays here and stays UNKNOWN rather than becoming REJECTED: removing a model verifies nothing about its licence, so if this ID is ever pulled again the licence is still unread and the same gate applies. The machine now has ZERO Ollama models installed.

entries.name: U^2-Net salient object detection weights (via rembg)
entries.source: downloaded by rembg on first run to ~/.u2net/u2net.onnx (176 MB)
entries.redistribution_rules: Apache-2.0 permits redistribution; the weights are not committed to this repo
entries.verified_by: Claude Code - U^2-Net is published under Apache-2.0 and rembg ships it under that licence
entries.notes: Segmentation, NOT generation. This is what makes a real 도리 sprite possible on a machine with no dedicated GPU: the reference images already contain the finished character, so it only has to be separated from its background - about a second per image on the CPU. Section 8 wants weights licensed separately from code, so this entry is separate from the rembg entry below. Output is a derivative of the USER'S reference image, whose own licence is covered by user-character-reference-images above.

entries.source: pip install rembg[cpu]

entries.name: Stable Diffusion v1.5 (weights)
entries.source: Hugging Face, downloaded by diffusers to ~/.cache/huggingface
entries.redistribution_rules: OpenRAIL-M permits redistribution of the weights and of derivatives if the same use-based restrictions are passed on. The weights are NOT committed to this repo; only generated PNGs are.
entries.verified_by: Claude Code - OpenRAIL-M explicitly permits commercial use; its restrictions are use-based (no illegal, harassing or deceptive output), none of which a hedgehog runner engages
entries.notes: Runs on the CPU in this container - minutes per 512px image, no GPU. Section 9 wanted the exact repository licence read before installation, and this is that check. Two limits recorded honestly rather than discovered later: (1) the model has never seen 도리, so txt2img produces A hedgehog, not THE one - a fixed seed is what makes a set of frames consistent with each other. (2) img2img preserves identity far better but cannot reliably rotate a front view into a side profile. Whether any output is usable is a human call under section 30. Alternatives considered and rejected: SD-Turbo and SDXL-Turbo are FASTER but ship under Stability's non-commercial research licence, so they are unusable here; FLUX.1-schnell is Apache-2.0 and would be preferable on licence grounds, but at 12B parameters it does not fit this machine's memory for CPU inference.

entries.name: Hugging Face diffusers / transformers / accelerate (code)
entries.source: pip
entries.redistribution_rules: Apache-2.0; build-time tool, not shipped in the APK
entries.notes: Section 8: the inference CODE is Apache-2.0, which says nothing about the WEIGHTS it loads - those are the separate stable-diffusion-v1-5 entry above. Driven by AI_GAME_COMPANY/tools/generate-sprite.py.

entries.name: Qwen-Image (20B MMDiT text-to-image)
entries.source: Hugging Face
entries.redistribution_rules: Apache-2.0 permits redistribution; weights not committed here
entries.verified_by: Claude Code - Apache-2.0 confirmed via published model documentation
entries.notes: Licence is excellent - Apache-2.0 is more permissive than SD 1.5's OpenRAIL-M, with no use-based restrictions. It is the HARDWARE that rules it out, and the numbers are checked in code by HardwareProfile.image_model_fit('qwen-image') rather than asserted here: about 18.5 GB of working set (14 GB for the DiT at GGUF Q4_K_M plus ~4.5 GB for the 8.3B text encoder) against 15.71 GB of TOTAL system RAM on a machine with no dedicated VRAM. Larger than the whole machine. The Q2_K variant at ~12.5 GB clears total RAM but not the free-RAM budget, and degrades quality. Beyond memory there is a second wall: a diffusion transformer runs its full 20B parameters at EVERY sampling step, so even swapped in, one image on this CPU would take hours rather than minutes. Revisit if a 24 GB+ VRAM machine appears; the licence will not be the obstacle.

entries.name: ComfyUI (node-graph diffusion runner)
entries.source: https://github.com/comfyanonymous/ComfyUI
entries.redistribution_rules: GPL-3.0 is copyleft, but that binds distribution of ComfyUI itself. It is a build-time tool here and is never bundled into the APK, so the copyleft obligation does not reach the game.
entries.notes: Model-agnostic: ComfyUI is a graph runner, so it is usable on this machine even though Qwen-Image is not. Pairing it with a model that fits (SD 1.5) works; pairing it with Qwen-Image does not, and that is a memory fact rather than a ComfyUI limitation.

entries.name: IP-Adapter (image prompt adapter, h94/IP-Adapter)
entries.source: Hugging Face h94/IP-Adapter
entries.redistribution_rules: Apache-2.0; weights not committed to this repo
entries.verified_by: Claude Code - Apache-2.0 confirmed on the model repository
entries.notes: The piece that makes generating 도리 possible rather than generating a hedgehog. It conditions on the reference PICTURE, so the pose is free while the character is constrained. The 'plus' variant uses patch embeddings from OpenCLIP-ViT-H rather than one global embedding, which stays closer to the reference. Its image encoder is what pushes the float32 stack to ~7.8 GB and forces bfloat16 on this machine - see HardwareProfile.image_model_fit('sd-1.5-ipadapter').

entries.name: Qwen3-VL (vision-language, served locally by Ollama)
entries.source: Pulled into local Ollama 0.33.3 by the project owner on 2026-09-10. Never sent anywhere: ollama_local_only is true and the client refuses a non-loopback endpoint.
entries.version: 8.8B parameters, Q4_K_M quantisation, 262144 context, 6.1 GB on disk (ollama show)
entries.redistribution_rules: Weights stay on this machine and are never bundled into the APK, so redistribution does not arise. Apache-2.0 would permit it with the notice if it ever did.
entries.notes: Licence read from the model's OWN shipped file, not inferred: `ollama show Qwen3-VL --license` prints the Apache License 2.0 text in full. Section 8 is explicit that 'it is a Qwen' is not evidence, and the registry already carries gemma4:26b as UNKNOWN for exactly that reason. Capabilities reported by ollama: completion, vision, tools, thinking - the vision half is the reason to prefer it over a text-only model here, since this project's open questions are about art on screen. RAM IS THE REAL LIMIT, NOT THE LICENCE: 6.1 GB of weights against 15.71 GB total, of which about 8.8 GB is already held by Windows and the editor, leaves 6.87 GB free - under the project's own free-minus-2GB budget of 4.87 GB. It does load and run (llama-server was observed at 6.8 GB resident), but it leaves under 1 GB free while loaded, which is the thrashing HardwareProfile.model_fit exists to refuse. A smaller Qwen3-VL tag (4B, roughly 3 GB) would fit with headroom.

pending_verification.reason: detect-environment.ps1 has now run, so the model IDs are known rather than hypothetical: gemma4:26b is the only one installed and has its own UNKNOWN entry above. Still pending is a model that actually fits this machine - a 7B-class Q4 (about 6 GB) is the largest tier 'orchestrator doctor' reports as runnable. Whichever ID is chosen needs its own entry before use; 'it is a Qwen' or 'it is a DeepSeek' is explicitly NOT sufficient to assume a licence.
Section 9: FLUX.1-schnell is a candidate only. Its exact repository licence must be read before installation, and weights are licensed separately from any inference code.
Section 10: TripoSR or similar. Licence unverified, and section 38 forbids calling a raw mesh a finished humanoid character.
Section 10 Route B needs a base character with a licence permitting commercial use and modification. None selected yet.
